english.title: Employment business request / receive fee from employee for finding / seeking to find another person
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person carrying on an employment business,

(A)_[requested]_
(B)_[directly or indirectly received]_

a fee from an employee, namely **(..SPECIFY THE EMPLOYEE..), for providing services for the purpose of finding or seeking to find another person, with a view to the employee acting for and under the control of that other person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6(1)(b) and (2) of the Employment Agencies Act 1973.

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 11B of the Employment Agencies Act 1973 provides that the court in which a person is convicted of an offence under this Act may order him to pay to the Secretary of State a sum which appears to the court not to exceed the costs of the investigation which resulted in the conviction.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
